findings.finding: Smcdeleg/Ssccfg depend on Sscsrind (per smcdeleg.adoc line 32). FreeBSD does not implement Sscsrind: no CSR definitions for siselect (0x150), sireg (0x151), sireg2-sireg6 (0x152-0x156) exist in encoding.h. Without Sscsrind, the indirect CSR access mechanism required by Smcdeleg/Ssccfg cannot function.
findings.snippet: No siselect/sireg* CSR definitions found in encoding.h.

spec_citations.excerpt: The Smcdeleg and Ssccfg extensions both depend on the Sscsrind extension.

The machine-level extension Smcsrind encompasses all added CSRs and all behavior modifications for a hart, over all privilege levels. For a supervisor-level environment, extension Sscsrind is essentially the same as Smcsrind except excluding the machine-level CSRs and behavior not directly visible to supervisor level.

findings.finding: No ISA extension string parsing for 'Sscsrind', 'Smcdeleg', or 'Ssccfg' exists. The kernel cannot detect whether the hardware supports these extensions, making it impossible to conditionally enable counter delegation or indirect CSR access.
findings.snippet: No Sscsrind/Smcdeleg/Ssccfg feature detection in identcpu.c.

spec_citations.excerpt: Smcdeleg/Ssccfg Counter Delegation Extensions, Version 1.0. These extensions provide a means for M-mode to allow writing select counters and event selectors from S/HS-mode.

findings.finding: bhyve VMM does not virtualize siselect/sireg* CSRs for guests, nor does it handle menvcfg.CDE delegation. The vmmops_delegate function only handles hedeleg/hideleg (HS-mode delegation), not mcdeleg (counter delegation). Guest access to delegated counters via indirect CSR would either trap incorrectly or leak host state.
findings.snippet: VMM delegate only handles hedeleg/hideleg; no mcdeleg or siselect/sireg* virtualization.

spec_citations.excerpt: When the Smcdeleg/Ssccfg extensions are enabled (menvcfg.CDE=1), it further allows M-mode to delegate select counters to S-mode. The siselect (and vsiselect) index range 0x40-0x5F is reserved for delegated counter access.

findings.finding: Context switch code does not save/restore siselect or sireg* CSRs. If Sscsrind were implemented, each process/thread would need its own virtualized view of these indirect CSR windows, requiring explicit save/restore on context switch. Currently not needed since the extension is unimplemented.
findings.snippet: No siselect/sireg* save/restore in context switch path.

spec_citations.excerpt: The value of miselect determines which register is accessed upon read or write of each of the machine indirect alias CSRs.
